[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#decision-summary]

## Decision Summary

Synopsys Polaris is designated as the enterprise application security testing platform, providing Coverity for Static Application Security Testing (SAST) and Black Duck for Software Composition Analysis (SCA). All development teams must use Polaris/Coverity for SAST scanning and Polaris/Black Duck for SCA scanning integrated into CI/CD pipelines.

---
page_texts.5:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Gainwell handles **Protected Health Information (PHI)** and **Personally Identifiable Information (PII)** across state Medicaid and healthcare programs. Application-layer vulnerabilities are a primary attack vector for data breaches in healthcare. HIPAA, FedRAMP, and state contract requirements mandate documented, repeatable application security testing practices.

The organization has made a procurement decision to license **Synopsys Polaris**, a unified cloud-based application security platform that combines:

- **Coverity** — a SAST engine with analysis support for major enterprise languages and frameworks
- **Black Duck** — an SCA engine for open-source vulnerability detection, license compliance, and Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) generation

This ADR documents that procurement decision, the alternatives that were evaluated, the organizational drivers, and the consequences for engineering teams.
page_texts.6:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

Key environmental characteristics relevant to this decision:

- Development spans multiple technology stacks (Java, .NET, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go)
- CI/CD pipelines run on Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions
- Applications are deployed on AWS across multiple accounts
- SBOM generation is required for federal contract compliance (Executive Order 14028, CMS requirements)
- License compliance scanning is required for open-source governance (see ADR-TEC-017)
- The organization had no centralized SAST or SCA platform prior to this procurement
page_texts.7:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Without a designated enterprise SAST and SCA platform, application security testing was ad hoc: individual teams selected tools independently, creating inconsistent coverage, fragmented reporting, duplicated licensing costs, and no unified security posture view across the application portfolio. A single, organizationally-committed platform is required to standardize practice and enable consistent enforcement of security gates.
page_texts.8:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#decision-drivers]

### Decision Drivers

- 🔒 **HIPAA Compliance**: §164.308(a)(1) requires ongoing risk analysis, including identification of application vulnerabilities
- 📋 **Federal SBOM Requirements**: Executive Order 14028 and CMS contracts require SBOM generation in standard formats (CycloneDX, SPDX)
- 🏢 **Existing Procurement**: Synopsys Polaris has been purchased; the organization has active licensing
- 🔄 **Consistency**: Eliminate tool fragmentation; establish a single source of truth for SAST and SCA findings
- 🔗 **CI/CD Integration**: Tools must integrate into Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions pipelines with quality gate enforcement
- 🧩 **Language Coverage**: Coverity supports the full range of languages in the Gainwell portfolio
- 🛡️ **Open-Source Risk**: Black Duck provides comprehensive open-source vulnerability and license risk visibility aligned with ADR-TEC-017 governance requirements

---
page_texts.10:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#polaris--coverity-sast-and-black-duck-sca]

### Polaris — Coverity (SAST) and Black Duck (SCA)

**Polaris SHALL be the enterprise application security testing platform. All in-scope applications must use Coverity for SAST scanning and Black Duck for SCA scanning, integrated into CI/CD pipelines.**
page_texts.12:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#polariscoverity--sast]

##### Polaris/Coverity — SAST

**Scope**: All custom-developed applications regardless of language or framework.

**Mandatory Integration Points**

| Integration Point | Requirement |
|-------------------|-------------|
| IDE Plugin | Coverity plugin SHALL be installed in approved developer IDEs for real-time feedback |
| Pull Request | Coverity scan SHALL run on every pull request; results visible in PR review |
| Build Pipeline | Coverity scan SHALL run on every build in CI/CD; build fails on new critical/high findings |
| Policy Configuration | Polaris policies SHALL be configured to enforce OWASP Top 10 and CWE Top 25 rule sets |

**Quality Gate Thresholds**

> **Authoritative Source**: The table below is the definitive quality gate threshold specification for Polaris/Coverity. The guidance document GUID-SEC-APP-SEC-Testing-2.7.02 references these values; any future changes must be made here first.

| Pipeline Stage | Critical | High | Medium | Low |
|----------------|----------|------|--------|-----|
| Development (IDE) | Warn | Warn | Info | Info |
| Staging | Block | Warn | Info | Info |
| Production | Block | Block | Warn | Info |

New findings (introduced since baseline) apply to gate enforcement. Legacy baseline findings are tracked separately and assigned to a remediation backlog.
page_texts.13:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#polarisblack-duck--sca]

##### Polaris/Black Duck — SCA

**Scope**: All applications using third-party libraries or open-source components.

**Mandatory Integration Points**

| Integration Point | Requirement |
|-------------------|-------------|
| Build Pipeline | Black Duck scan SHALL run on every build; results include CVE findings and license classification |
| SBOM Generation | Black Duck SHALL generate SBOMs in CycloneDX format for all production builds |
| Continuous Monitoring | Black Duck policy notifications SHALL be enabled to alert on newly disclosed CVEs affecting deployed components |
| License Compliance | Black Duck license policies SHALL flag copyleft and restricted licenses per ADR-TEC-017 |

**Package Manager Coverage**

Black Duck must be configured to scan all package managers in use: npm, NuGet, Maven, PyPI, Go modules, and any others added to the portfolio.
page_texts.14:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#polaris-connect-api]

##### Polaris Connect API

The Polaris Connect REST API provides programmatic access to scan results, policy violations, and finding metadata. Teams MAY use the Polaris Connect API to:

- Pull finding data into centralized vulnerability management dashboards
- Integrate finding creation into issue trackers (Azure Boards, Jira)
- Build custom reporting against the Polaris data model
page_texts.15:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#environment-promotion-requirement]

##### Environment Promotion Requirement

All Polaris configurations (policy settings, quality gate thresholds, rule customizations) must be tested in a lower environment before applying to pipelines serving production workloads.

---
page_texts.16:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#rollout-sequencing--policy-tuning-before-blocking-gates]

##### Rollout Sequencing — Policy Tuning Before Blocking Gates

Blocking quality gate thresholds (Critical and High) **MUST NOT be activated** for a given application until both of the following conditions are satisfied:

1. **Baseline established**: A full Polaris/Coverity scan has been completed for the application and all findings catalogued. The baseline captures the pre-migration vulnerability state and is used to distinguish new findings from legacy debt.
2. **Policy tuning review completed**: A minimum **two-week policy tuning period** has been observed following the initial baseline scan, during which:
   - Rule configurations are adjusted to eliminate systematic false positives
   - All remaining flagged findings are reviewed for validity
   - A nominated security engineer reviews the tuned finding set and formally signs off that blocking gate enforcement is appropriate

Quality gates in **Warn** mode may be activated at any time after baseline establishment to provide developer feedback without blocking pipelines.

This sequencing requirement is mandatory. Activating blocking gates before the tuning review is complete is a deviation requiring a documented exception approved by the Application Security Team lead.

---
page_texts.17:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#migration-requirements]

##### Migration Requirements

All development teams currently using SAST or SCA tools other than Polaris/Coverity and Polaris/Black Duck must migrate to Polaris by the timelines and under the process defined below.

**Migration Deadline**

All in-scope applications must have Polaris/Coverity (SAST) and Polaris/Black Duck (SCA) integrated into their CI/CD pipelines within **180 days of the acceptance date of this ADR (by 2026-10-20)**. Applications onboarding after the acceptance date of this ADR must integrate Polaris from initial pipeline setup.

**Migration Ownership**

The **DevSecOps Engineering team**, in coordination with the **Application Security team**, is responsible for:

- Providing pipeline integration templates for Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions (see GUID-SEC-APP-SEC-Testing-2.7.02 for reference configurations)
- Advising individual application teams during their baseline establishment and policy tuning phases
- Tracking migration status across the portfolio and reporting progress to security leadership monthly

Application teams are responsible for executing the migration within their pipelines and completing the mandatory baseline and tuning steps before activating blocking gates.

**Transition Period Guidance**

During the transition period (from ADR acceptance until a team's migration deadline), teams that have not yet migrated to Polaris must:

- Continue operating any existing SAST/SCA tooling without removing coverage
- Not adopt new non-Polaris SAST or SCA tools
- Submit a migration plan to the DevSecOps Engineering team within **30 days of this ADR's acceptance date**

Teams that cannot meet the 180-day migration deadline due to documented technical constraints must submit a migration exception to the Application Security team lead for approval, including a revised target date.

---
page_texts.18:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#benefits]

#### Benefits

- Unified SAST and SCA platform under a single vendor relationship, reducing integration and operational overhead
- Coverity's inter-procedural analysis provides deeper code flow coverage than pattern-matching alternatives
- Black Duck's comprehensive open-source intelligence database supports both CVE detection and license compliance
- Polaris Connect API enables integration with existing vulnerability management and issue tracking tooling
- Cloud-hosted platform eliminates on-premises infrastructure management burden
page_texts.19:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#risks-and-mitigations]

#### Risks and Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Single-vendor dependency for two critical security functions | Polaris is a mature, widely-deployed platform; risk is accepted as proportional to procurement commitment |
| Pipeline performance impact from Coverity inter-procedural analysis | Use incremental analysis on branches; reserve full analysis for main/release builds |
| Policy tuning required to achieve acceptable false positive rates | Dedicate capacity in the implementation phase to tune rules before enforcing blocking gates |
| New vulnerability disclosures in Black Duck database triggering alerts | Establish triage SLA for newly disclosed CVEs; do not gate pipelines on non-critical findings without review |

---
page_texts.21:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#option-a-veracode]

### Option A: Veracode

**Description**: Veracode provides a cloud-based platform for SAST (Static Analysis), SCA (Software Composition Analysis), DAST, and penetration testing. Veracode uses a binary/bytecode submission model for SAST analysis.

**Pros**:

- ✅ Broad language support including legacy platforms
- ✅ Established track record in regulated industries
- ✅ Single-vendor platform covering SAST, SCA, and DAST

**Cons**:

- ❌ Binary submission model introduces longer scan cycle times compared to source-based analysis
- ❌ No active procurement relationship; licensing would require a new procurement process
- ❌ Higher per-scan cost model for large portfolios

**Verdict**: ❌ Rejected — No existing procurement; Polaris is already licensed

---
page_texts.22:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#option-b-checkmarx-one]

### Option B: Checkmarx One

**Description**: Checkmarx One is a cloud-native application security platform providing SAST, SCA (via Checkmarx SCA), and API security testing.

**Pros**:

- ✅ Strong SAST engine with incremental scanning capability
- ✅ Unified platform across SAST and SCA
- ✅ Azure DevOps integration

**Cons**:

- ❌ No active procurement relationship; licensing would require a new procurement process
- ❌ Less mature SCA open-source intelligence database compared to Black Duck
- ❌ Displacing an existing licensed platform would incur duplicate cost during transition

**Verdict**: ❌ Rejected — No existing procurement; Polaris is already licensed

---
page_texts.23:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#option-c-snyk]

### Option C: Snyk

**Description**: Snyk is a developer-first security platform focused primarily on SCA (open-source vulnerability and license scanning) with SAST capability added via Snyk Code.

**Pros**:

- ✅ Developer-friendly UX with strong IDE integration
- ✅ Broad package manager support
- ✅ Fast SCA scanning well-suited to CI pipelines

**Cons**:

- ❌ Snyk Code SAST is less mature than Coverity for enterprise inter-procedural analysis
- ❌ No active procurement relationship; licensing would require a new procurement process
- ❌ Per-contributor pricing can become expensive at enterprise scale
- ❌ Acquiring a separate SAST platform would be required; Snyk alone does not replace Coverity

**Verdict**: ❌ Rejected — No existing procurement; Snyk Code does not provide equivalent SAST depth to Coverity; Polaris is already licensed

---
page_texts.24:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#option-d-fragmented-best-of-breed-no-standard]

### Option D: Fragmented Best-of-Breed (No Standard)

**Description**: Allow each development team to independently select SAST and SCA tools based on team preference and project requirements. No enterprise standard mandated.

**Pros**:

- ✅ Teams choose tools optimized for their specific language and framework
- ✅ No transition cost from current practices

**Cons**:

- ❌ No unified security posture visibility across the application portfolio
- ❌ Inconsistent quality gate enforcement; teams may have no gates at all
- ❌ License compliance risk — teams may not consistently perform license scanning
- ❌ Duplicated tooling costs across teams
- ❌ Compliance reporting is fragmented and difficult to aggregate for audits

**Verdict**: ❌ Rejected — Inconsistent practice is incompatible with regulatory compliance and enterprise security governance obligations

---
page_texts.25:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#decision-outcome]

## Decision Outcome

**Selected Option**: Polaris — Coverity (SAST) and Black Duck (SCA)
page_texts.26:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#justification]

### Justification

> *The organization has purchased Synopsys Polaris, providing both Coverity (SAST) and Black Duck (SCA) under an active licensing agreement. No equivalent competing platform is currently licensed.*

All alternative options were evaluated and rejected because they require new procurement to replace a platform that is already licensed and available. The fragmented approach was rejected because it is incompatible with consistent compliance reporting and enterprise security governance. Polaris satisfies the language coverage, CI/CD integration, SBOM generation, and license compliance requirements that are mandatory for the Gainwell portfolio.
page_texts.27:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#vendor-governance]

### Vendor Governance

Polaris represents a single-vendor dependency for both SAST (Coverity) and SCA (Black Duck). The following provisions govern that dependency and ensure portability.

**Re-evaluation Triggers**

This ADR must be formally re-evaluated if any of the following conditions arise:

- Synopsys licensing renewal fails or cannot be completed on commercially acceptable terms
- Synopsys is acquired and the acquisition materially affects product roadmap, licensing terms, or support continuity
- The sustained false-positive rate for Coverity findings (averaged across three or more production applications over a 90-day period post-tuning) exceeds 40% of all Critical/High findings
- Polaris loses support for a primary language in the Gainwell portfolio (Java, .NET, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go) without a committed remediation roadmap
- An alternative platform demonstrably provides superior coverage and CI/CD integration at equivalent or lower total cost of ownership

Re-evaluation is initiated by the Application Security team lead and reviewed by Enterprise Architecture before any procurement change is made.

**Finding Data Export Requirements**

The Polaris procurement agreement must include contractual provisions for data export. Teams must maintain access to:

- SAST findings exportable in JSON or CSV format via the Polaris Connect API or platform bulk export at any time during the contract term
- SCA findings and SBOM artifacts exportable in CycloneDX (preferred) or SPDX formats — open standards consumable by any successor tooling without vendor-specific transformation
- Historical finding data with a minimum 24-month retention period, available for export on contract termination

**Open Standards and Data Portability**

By mandating CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM generation and Polaris Connect API integration, this ADR ensures that security findings and SBOM artifacts remain platform-independent. Teams must not store security findings exclusively within Polaris — open findings must be tracked in a platform-independent issue tracker (Azure Boards or Jira) to prevent data lock-in and to maintain finding history across any future platform transition.
page_texts.28:
[decisions/security/ADR-SEC-002-application-security-testing-platform.md#consequences]

### Consequences

**Positive** ✅

- Single platform for SAST and SCA across the portfolio; consistent findings, policies, and reporting
- Black Duck satisfies the SCA requirement in ADR-TEC-017 for open-source scanning and license tracking
- SBOM generation via Black Duck fulfills federal SBOM requirements without additional tooling
- Polaris Connect API enables integration with existing vulnerability management infrastructure

**Negative** ⚠️

- Teams using other SAST/SCA tools must migrate to Polaris; migration involves pipeline reconfiguration and baseline establishment
- Coverity's inter-procedural analysis requires adequate compute capacity in CI/CD agents; build times will increase
- Policy tuning investment is required to achieve acceptable false positive rates before enforcement gates are enabled

**Neutral** ℹ️

- DAST and penetration testing are out of scope for this ADR; existing guidance and tools continue to apply
- Teams may supplement Polaris with additional open-source tooling (e.g., secrets detection via Gitleaks) where Polaris does not provide coverage
